questions.question: Why does electricity cost money? Give three costs that are part of the price.
questions.expected_answer: A huge system is needed to make and deliver electricity. Costs include building infrastructure, like power stations, coal mines, power lines, pylons, substations, transformers and meters; running costs, like coal, paying workers, and repairing and replacing machines and stolen cables; and the cost of pollution. These are paid by people who buy electricity, measured in units called kilowatt-hours.

questions.question: Which appliances use the most electricity and why? What else affects how much an appliance uses?
questions.expected_answer: Appliances that make heat use the most, like the geyser, heater, stove, kettle, iron and hair dryer, because making heat from electricity takes a lot of energy. In many homes the geyser uses the most. The power in watts on the label and how long the appliance is switched on also affect how much electricity it uses.

questions.question: Give five ways to save electricity at home and two reasons why saving matters.
questions.expected_answer: Switch off lights and appliances when not in use and switch off at the wall; use LED bulbs; boil only the water you need; take short showers; put a blanket on the geyser or use a solar water heater; cook with lids on; keep the fridge door closed; wear warm clothes before using a heater; dry washing in the sun. Saving reduces the family's bill, means less coal is burned and less pollution, and lowers the risk of load shedding.
